key_insight: Adding an AI teammate changes not just task performance, but the way human teammates talk to each other. In small-team decision-making, the AI’s presence can reshape communication patterns, social dynamics, and how humans coordinate under pressure.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the gap in understanding how conversational AI affects human-human communication when it is treated as a teammate rather than a tool. It examines whether AI changes team discourse and sociocognitive dynamics during collaborative decisions.
method: Ran a randomized controlled study with small teams completing a high-stakes moral-dilemma decision task.
Compared teams of two students plus an AI teammate against all-human teams.
Analyzed team interaction using Group Communication Analysis (GCA), team surveys, and lexical analysis of the conversation transcripts.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows that deploying AI as a teammate can have social side effects beyond accuracy or efficiency. Designers should evaluate communication quality, trust, coordination, and human-team cohesion—not just task outcomes.
visual_elements: Split-screen team diagram: all-human team vs. human+AI team
Conversation flow map showing shifts in speaking patterns and turn-taking
Bar chart or radar chart comparing communication metrics between conditions
Icon set for trust, coordination, conflict, and decision pressure
paper_title: The Social Cost of an AI Teammate: How an Artificial Teammate Reshapes Human-Human Communication in Small-Team Decision-Making
paper_authors: Nia Nixon, Jaeyoon Choi, Pedro Martins De Bastos, Mohammad Amin Samadi, Luise Mehner
